Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a head-to-head client benchmark vs runtime yesterday and saw surprising results. grpc client had better tail than REST even at same qps. I think client-side keepalive / conn-pool and Nagle/TLS overhead are skewing numbers. Dumping notes here.

Maya Patel: Oof. can you paste the harness + cmds you used? want to reproduce locally.

Alex Chen: Yep. two runs:
```
# REST (http/1.1)
w rk -t12 -c200 -d60s --latency --script=client.lua http://api.internal/v1/generate
# gRPC (http/2)
ghz --insecure -c 200 -n 20000 api.internal:50051 inference.Generate
```
Also tried curl with parallel connections and python requests loop. Noticed headers: `Connection: keep-alive` toggles made a big difference.

Kevin Zhao: Important: was TLS terminated at edge (envoy/lb) for both? http/2 vs http/1.1 differences can hide in LB behavior.

Alex Chen: TLS was terminated at our edge Envoy for REST; gRPC test used direct http2 to runtime (bypassed edge for the experiment). Logs show lots of TLS handshakes during REST run:
```
edge-proxy TLS handshakes: 3242/sec
edge-proxy new conns: 187/sec
```
which smells like connection churn + no session reuse.

Samantha Ortiz: Try disabling Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) on client sockets. In a past test, disabling Nagle gave ~20% lower p95 for many small responses (single-token finishes).

Maya Patel: Also check client pool defaults: python `requests` Session default pool size is 10 per host; our wrk script opened 200 concurrent clients which caused connection storms. Which SDKs did you try?

Alex Chen: Tests: `requests` (sync), `httpx` (async), `grpc` Go client. The `requests` run spawned many short-lived connections because the harness created a new Session per thread. snippet: `for t in threads: s = requests.Session(); s.post(...)`. That was my bug — should reuse Session.

Kevin Zhao: Another angle: KV cache behavior on runtime. When the KV cache hits, model work is tiny so network/TLS dominates. When cache miss, model time dwarfs network and the client differences mostly vanish. We saw that in profiling.

Alex Chen: Profiling summary (approx):
- REST (new connections): p50 120ms, p95 320ms
- REST (keepalive + pooled): p50 60ms, p95 110ms
- gRPC (pooled, http2): p50 55ms, p95 95ms
- Cache-miss (both): p95 ~ 800ms (model time dominates)
So for cached short responses, connection behavior changes everything.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback v1.12.3 triggered (perf regression)

Maya Patel: Proposed standard methodology for apples-to-apples: 
1) Ensure same TLS termination path (either both go through envoy or both bypass).
2) Match HTTP versions (http/2 vs http/1.1) or explicitly test differences.
3) Fix client settings: connection reuse, pool size, TCP_NODELAY toggle, TLS session reuse.
4) Warm up runtime until steady-state (kv caches populated, kernels JITed).
5) Use replay harness from prod traces for realistic tokens + sequence lengths.
6) Collect tcpdump + envoy metrics + runtime perf counters.

Kevin Zhao: Add: disable client-side Nagle if responses are < ~1KB, ensure TLS session reuse (session tickets) and connection TTLs emulate real clients. Also include long-run (10m+) to see autoscaling/eviction effects.

Alex Chen: I'll write a short runbook and add a standardized benchmark client to perf repo (node/python/grpc variants) so future comparisons are fair. TL;DR: client config matters — default libs bias toward new connections and that can flip conclusions about kernel / batching perf. :memo:

Samantha Ortiz: sg. if you want I can add a small patch to node SDK to expose `tcpNoDelay: true` and sane pool defaults. ping me and I'll PR.

Maya Patel: Thanks Alex — pls drop the final commands + a minimal reproducer here once you push. I'll start a quick run against emulated prod trace.

Alex Chen: Will do, pushing to perf/benchmarks today. If anyone else has edge-case things (HTTP/2 proxy misconfigs, Windows Nagle defaults), add them to the thread.
